summary: Returns paginated award or subaward search rows for a filtered advanced-search population. Live award-mode probing confirmed the default spending_level=awards plus helper identifiers such as generated_internal_id, and a richer 2026-05-14 contract outlier screen confirmed that requested rows can also carry date, agency, sub-agency, and contract-type context before drilldown; the raw award-mode body materially surfaces generated_internal_id, and this bundle models canonical_award_lookup_id as a derived-only semantic alias for that same returned value rather than as a second live payload key for downstream award drilldowns. Reviewer-backed story evidence also shows that bounded time_period screens are activity screens: FY2026 dashboard screening surfaced legacy award DEAC3243AL00036 for the Regents of the University of California with Start Date 1978-09-30, End Date 2006-05-31, and Award Amount 35295689219.18, so Award Amount must not be read as current-period spend. Endpoint-level semanticAffordances now declare the canonical_award_lookup_id handoff, the Award Amount activity-screen warning, and follow-up paths into v2__awards__award_id or v2__awards__funding so runtime can surface them structurally instead of leaving them prose-only.
businessPurpose: Use this endpoint when you need to inspect the actual award or subaward records behind a complex advanced-search filter set. It is the row-level drilldown surface for the broader USAspending advanced-search system.
analyticalGrain: One result row per matching prime award by default, or one result row per matching subaward when spending_level=subawards or subawards=true.

primaryEntities.name: Prime award row
primaryEntities.description: A single filtered award returned in award mode with requested display columns plus helper identifiers such as internal_id and generated_internal_id.

primaryEntities.name: Subaward row
primaryEntities.description: A single filtered subaward returned in subaward mode with requested subaward labels plus prime-award linkage helpers.

primaryEntities.name: Advanced-search filter population
primaryEntities.description: The underlying set of awards or subawards selected by AdvancedFilterObject before projection and pagination are applied.

measures.name: Award Amount
measures.description: Prime-award monetary amount available for supported award families when requested. In bounded high-value screens, this remains the award-level amount on each returned row rather than a period-only subtotal or current-period spend figure, and the search row does not identify the specific current-period transaction or modification that caused inclusion. Reviewer-backed FY2026 screening surfaced Regents award DEAC3243AL00036 with Award Amount 35295689219.18 despite Start Date 1978-09-30 and End Date 2006-05-31.

measures.name: Total Outlays
measures.description: Prime-award outlay measure available for supported award families when requested.

measures.name: Loan Value and Subsidy Cost
measures.description: Loan/assistance measures available on the relevant award families when requested.

measures.name: Sub-Award Amount
measures.description: Subaward monetary amount available in subaward mode when requested.

measures.name: DEFC-specific obligation and outlay fields
measures.description: COVID-19 and infrastructure obligation/outlay fields can appear when requested and when the underlying row has matching DEFC data.

dimensions.name: Award versus subaward mode
dimensions.description: spending_level and subawards determine whether results represent prime awards or subawards.

dimensions.name: Requested field catalog
dimensions.description: The fields array controls which business columns are projected into each row and therefore shapes the response schema.

dimensions.name: Advanced search filters
dimensions.description: The shared AdvancedFilterObject lets callers slice by time, agencies, recipient/location criteria, award types, program filters, NAICS/PSC/TAS, and disaster codes before row retrieval.

dimensions.name: Award family
dimensions.description: Contracts, IDVs, loans, non-loan assistance, and subaward families expose different valid field labels and measures.

dimensions.name: Canonical award lookup id
dimensions.description: For prime-award rows, the raw search body materially exposes generated_internal_id rather than a literal canonical_award_lookup_id property. This bundle normalizes that same returned string as results[].canonical_award_lookup_id for downstream handoff into v2__awards__award_id or v2__awards__funding, but the alias is derived-only in the semantic bundle rather than surfaced as a second live response field.

dimensions.name: Activity-screen period interpretation
dimensions.description: Bounded time_period filters on this search surface act as activity screens, not current-period subtotal calculators. Requested Start Date, End Date, and Last Modified Date are screening clues about award vintage and recency, but the search row does not name the specific transaction, modification, or funding event that caused period inclusion and it does not convert Award Amount into a period-only measure. Reviewer-backed FY2026 compact-dashboard evidence surfaced Regents award DEAC3243AL00036 with Start Date 1978-09-30, End Date 2006-05-31, Last Modified Date 2026-05-06 14:28:38, and Award Amount 35295689219.18, showing that clearly legacy awards can still appear in a bounded period screen when later activity keeps them in scope.

suitableQuestions.name: Which awards match this complex filter set?
suitableQuestions.description: Best for browsing actual award rows behind advanced search criteria instead of just counts or aggregates.

suitableQuestions.name: Which contract awards are highest-value in this filtered slice?
suitableQuestions.description: Use the bounded high_value_award_screening pattern for a thin leaderboard, or use contract_outlier_dashboard_screening when you want Award Amount leaders plus Start Date, End Date, Last Modified Date, Awarding/Funding Agency, Awarding/Funding Sub Agency, and Contract Award Type on the first screen. Capture generated_internal_id from the raw search row or read the same value as the bundle alias canonical_award_lookup_id before drilling into award detail or funding workflows. Verify award dates before describing hits as newly signed awards, because the bounded time_period can surface older long-running awards and Award Amount remains an award-level field.

suitableQuestions.name: Which high-value contract hits already look legacy, cross-agency, or otherwise outlier-worthy before drilldown?
suitableQuestions.description: Use contract_outlier_dashboard_screening to keep the search bounded while adding Start Date, End Date, Last Modified Date, Awarding/Funding Agency, Awarding/Funding Sub Agency, and Contract Award Type. Live evidence already separated an older Defense Health Agency Humana contract from a Department of Energy award funded by the Department of the Navy before any award-detail request, and reviewer-backed story evidence showed Regents award DEAC3243AL00036 appearing inside an FY2026 screen with Start Date 1978-09-30 and End Date 2006-05-31. Treat Award Amount on these rows as lifetime award size and use downstream detail or funding follow-up before narrating current-period spend.

suitableQuestions.name: Why did a legacy award appear in this bounded dashboard screen?
suitableQuestions.description: Use the compact outlier screen to identify legacy-looking rows, but explain period inclusion through follow-up rather than from Award Amount alone. The search row can show that a legacy award was still relevant to the bounded activity screen; use award detail to confirm award vintage and funding follow-up when you need a current-period interpretation or dashboard-safe measure.

suitableQuestions.name: Who are the top recipients or agencies in a filtered slice?
suitableQuestions.description: Request recipient, agency, and amount fields, then sort and paginate through the matching rows.

suitableQuestions.name: Which subawards sit under a filtered prime-award population?
suitableQuestions.description: Switch to spending_level=subawards and request subaward labels plus prime-award linkage fields.

suitableQuestions.name: Which award rows should I inspect further in award detail APIs?
suitableQuestions.description: Use this endpoint to identify candidate rows and capture the raw generated_internal_id value, which this bundle normalizes as canonical_award_lookup_id for downstream award detail or funding lookups.

notSuitableFor.name: Ready-made aggregates or totals
notSuitableFor.description: This endpoint returns rows, not grouped summaries. Use aggregate endpoints when the question is about totals by geography, time, or award type.

notSuitableFor.name: Bulk export of very large result sets
notSuitableFor.description: Deep pagination becomes a sequential search_after workflow and may be a poor fit for full-population extraction.

notSuitableFor.name: Earlier-than-search-floor historical coverage
notSuitableFor.description: The shared search system can emit warnings about the earliest searchable date and may require download workflows for older history.

notSuitableFor.name: Questions that need fields you did not request
notSuitableFor.description: The response is projection-driven, so omitted columns are absent rather than implicitly available.

notSuitableFor.name: Current-period spend dashboards built from Award Amount alone
notSuitableFor.description: Do not read row-level Award Amount as the spend subtotal for the bounded time_period. Reviewer-backed FY2026 screening returned legacy Regents award DEAC3243AL00036 with 1978 start and 2006 end dates, and the search row still did not reveal the specific FY2026 transaction or modification that caused inclusion, so current-period interpretation requires downstream detail or funding follow-up.

joins.description: Treat this bundle-derived semantic alias as the canonical award handoff key. In raw prime-award search results, read generated_internal_id; in this bundle, normalize that same string as canonical_award_lookup_id; then pass it unchanged to v2__awards__award_id path award_id or v2__awards__funding body award_id, and expect award detail to echo the same business key as generated_unique_award_id. Do not wait for raw search output to materialize both names: canonical_award_lookup_id is the bundle alias for the generated_internal_id value already returned.

generated_internal_id is the literal transport field in raw search responses. This bundle normalizes that same value as canonical_award_lookup_id. If you are reading raw JSON, use generated_internal_id; if you are reading the semantic bundle, treat the same string as canonical_award_lookup_id; then pass it unchanged to v2__awards__award_id path award_id or v2__awards__funding body award_id. Do not treat the two names as separate ids.
When Awarding Agency is requested, rows may also include agency_slug that can support agency-profile linking when a profile page exists.

Subaward mode returns prime-award linkage helpers; when present, treat prime_award_generated_internal_id as the prime-award canonical_award_lookup_id for downstream prime-award detail or funding workflows.

workflows.name: Screen for high-value contract awards
workflows.description: Use the high-value contract screening template to surface top-dollar contract candidates quickly, then carry the canonical handoff value from the chosen row into downstream detail workflows: in raw output this appears as generated_internal_id, and the bundle normalizes it as canonical_award_lookup_id. Interpret the bounded time_period as an activity screen, not as a guarantee that returned awards were newly signed in that period.

steps.action: Start from the high_value_award_screening request shape: contract award_type_codes A/B/C/D, a bounded time_period, page=1, limit=5, and the small visible field set Award ID / Recipient Name / Award Amount / Awarding Agency.
Sort by Award Amount in descending order so the first page surfaces top-dollar contract candidates rather than alphabetical Award ID rows.

Capture generated_internal_id from the selected award row; this bundle normalizes that same string as canonical_award_lookup_id for downstream handoff, even though the helper identifier is not part of the requested visible fields and the raw body does not include a literal canonical_award_lookup_id key. The selected AI-keyword competition story reconfirmed this raw-versus-alias split on live rows W911QX20C0023 and W911QX25C0002.

Before describing a hit as a new award in the bounded period, verify date_signed or period-of-performance dates in award detail: a bounded time_period screen can surface older long-running awards that are active in the period, while Award Amount remains an award-level value on the returned row.

Reuse the normalized handoff value unchanged in downstream award drilldowns: send generated_internal_id (or the same value as bundle alias canonical_award_lookup_id) as path award_id to v2__awards__award_id or as body award_id to v2__awards__funding; award detail may echo the same value as generated_unique_award_id.

workflows.name: Screen a compact contract outlier dashboard
workflows.description: Use one bounded high-value search call to surface top-dollar contract rows together with date and agency context before deciding which awards deserve deeper detail or funding drilldown. Treat the result as an activity-screen dashboard: rows can be legacy awards with later period activity, Award Amount is still lifetime award size rather than current-period spend, and the search row alone does not explain the specific in-period event that caused inclusion.

steps.action: Start from the contract_outlier_dashboard_screening request shape: contract award_type_codes A/B/C/D, a bounded time_period, page=1, limit=5, sort=Award Amount descending, and fields Award ID / Recipient Name / Award Amount / Awarding Agency / Awarding Sub Agency / Funding Agency / Funding Sub Agency / Contract Award Type / Start Date / End Date / Last Modified Date.

Use Start Date, End Date, and Last Modified Date together to classify each hit before drilldown, but do not treat those fields as a complete explanation for period inclusion. The live richer screen showed Humana HT940216C0001 as an older still-active award, and reviewer-backed story evidence also showed Regents DEAC3243AL00036 in the same FY2026-style screen with Start Date 1978-09-30, End Date 2006-05-31, and Last Modified Date 2026-05-06 14:28:38, proving that even clearly legacy awards can surface in a bounded period screen.

Compare Awarding Agency versus Funding Agency, and Awarding Sub Agency versus Funding Sub Agency, to surface cross-agency patterns directly in the search rows; the live richer screen showed Sandia DENA0003525 as Department of Energy-awarded but Department of Defense / Department of the Navy-funded.

Capture generated_internal_id from the selected award row; this bundle normalizes that same string as canonical_award_lookup_id for downstream handoff, and the richer screen preserved that helper even though it requested 11 visible screening columns.

If a high-value row looks legacy or already ended, hand the normalized award key into v2__awards__award_id before dashboarding it as current-period spending. Reviewer-backed follow-up for Regents DEAC3243AL00036 confirmed date_signed 1978-09-30 and period_of_performance.end_date 2006-05-31 even though the bounded FY2026 search row carried Award Amount 35295689219.18 and Last Modified Date 2026-05-06 14:28:38, so award detail is the checkpoint for confirming award vintage rather than assuming the bounded screen found a new award.

If the dashboard question is about current-period interpretation rather than lifetime award size, follow the legacy-confirmed award with v2__awards__funding or another downstream current-period evidence source instead of reusing Award Amount. Until that follow-up is complete, label Award Amount as lifetime award size on the matched award row and describe the hit only as an activity-screen match, not as a current-period spend subtotal.

workflows.name: Explain a legacy award in a bounded activity screen
workflows.description: Use this workflow when a bounded contract dashboard surfaces a row whose visible award dates look much older than the requested period. The goal is to explain why the row is relevant to the activity screen without mislabeling Award Amount as current-period spend.

steps.action: Start from the contract_outlier_dashboard_screening request or an equivalent bounded award search that includes Award Amount, Start Date, End Date, and Last Modified Date. If the visible dates look far older than the filter window, treat the row as a legacy-looking activity-screen hit.

Separate the two meanings immediately: Award Amount is lifetime award size on the matched award row, while bounded time_period membership only says the award had relevant activity or updates in the screened period. The Regents row DEAC3243AL00036 demonstrates this separation because the row carried Award Amount 35295689219.18 even though Start Date was 1978-09-30 and End Date was 2006-05-31.

Carry generated_internal_id from the raw row, or the same value as canonical_award_lookup_id in this bundle, into v2__awards__award_id to confirm date_signed and period_of_performance before describing the row as a current-period award.
If award detail confirms legacy dates, keep the search row labeled as a legacy award with current-period activity-screen relevance. Do not backfill Award Amount into a fiscal-year spend chart.

Only when the dashboard needs a current-period narrative or measure, continue to v2__awards__funding or another downstream current-period evidence source. Publish current-period claims from that follow-up evidence, not from the search row's Award Amount.

workflows.name: Preview awards before detailed follow-up
workflows.description: Build a narrow filter set, request only the columns you need, then carry the generated award handoff value from the selected row into downstream detail workflows; the raw search body labels it generated_internal_id and this bundle normalizes it as canonical_award_lookup_id. Reviewer-backed live evidence also confirmed a bounded keyword-led contract preview when filters.keywords is paired with explicit award_type_codes.

steps.action: Assemble the AdvancedFilterObject for the slice you want to inspect. For the reviewer-backed keyword preview path used before paired download, include explicit award_type_codes alongside filters.keywords; keywords=['forest'] with award_type_codes ['A','B','C','D'] returned 3 award rows.
Choose a small fields array plus sort/page/limit controls so the response schema stays interpretable and bounded.

Use generated_internal_id from raw prime-award search output for downstream award detail or funding workflows, or read the same value through this bundle's semantic alias canonical_award_lookup_id; in subaward mode use prime_award_generated_internal_id for the linked prime award when present. Raw callEndpoint output does not materialize canonical_award_lookup_id as a second field.

workflows.name: Sequential deep pagination
workflows.description: For deep result windows, replay the same request with the page_metadata cursor pair rather than assuming simple random page jumps remain valid.

steps.action: Request a bounded page and inspect page_metadata.hasNext plus the optional last_record cursor pair.
If another page is needed, send the same filters, fields, sort, and order together with both last_record_unique_id and last_record_sort_value.

caveats.statement: The response schema is caller-shaped by the fields array and varies across award families and subaward mode.
caveats.impact: Downstream code must not assume one universal row schema for all requests.

caveats.statement: Some requested labels return nested objects rather than simple scalars.
caveats.impact: Schema-on-read logic should handle object-valued cells such as NAICS, PSC, and location fields.

caveats.statement: The legacy subawards boolean and the spending_level selector both influence row grain.
caveats.impact: Be explicit about the desired mode so prime-award and subaward templates are not mixed accidentally.

caveats.statement: Live responses can warn that search start and end dates are currently limited to an earliest date of 2007-10-01.
caveats.impact: For older historical work, plan a download workflow rather than assuming this search surface covers the full 2000-forward window.

caveats.statement: Related award drilldown endpoints relabel the same handoff business key: raw search responses expose generated_internal_id, award detail may echo generated_unique_award_id, and funding expects that same value under request field award_id; canonical_award_lookup_id is this bundle's derived-only semantic alias for the raw search value, not a second live response key.
caveats.impact: Normalize the handoff value as canonical_award_lookup_id inside the semantic bundle, but if you inspect only the raw search body, read generated_internal_id and pass it unchanged downstream; do not substitute the display Award ID and do not wait for both handoff names to appear together in the live payload.

caveats.statement: A bounded time_period screen can return older long-running awards or even clearly legacy awards whose displayed start and end dates sit far outside the filter window. Reviewer-backed FY2026 compact-dashboard evidence returned Regents award DEAC3243AL00036 with Award Amount 35295689219.18, Start Date 1978-09-30, End Date 2006-05-31, and Last Modified Date 2026-05-06 14:28:38.
caveats.impact: Treat inclusion as evidence of current-period activity or update, not as proof of current-period spend or a newly signed award. Keep Award Amount labeled as lifetime award size until award-detail and related follow-up establish the current-period story.

caveats.statement: A richer contract-outlier screen can expose date and cross-agency context in one search call, but it still does not explain why a legacy row matched the bounded period or translate Award Amount into a current-period subtotal.
caveats.impact: Use the richer search template for first-pass dashboard screening, then confirm legacy-versus-current-period meaning in award detail and use funding follow-up when you need a current-period measure or explanation before narrating or charting the outlier.

caveats.statement: A bounded time_period search row does not identify the exact transaction, modification, or funding event that caused the award to appear in the screened period; it only proves the award was relevant to that activity screen.
caveats.impact: When a legacy row appears, explain the first screen as an activity-screen match and use award detail plus funding follow-up if you need a current-period reason or measure.

caveats.statement: Keyword-led preview is now observed for the bounded paired-download pattern when explicit award_type_codes are supplied alongside filters.keywords.
caveats.impact: If you are previewing a keyword-led download scope on this endpoint, include award_type_codes explicitly instead of assuming download defaults will carry over.
